QUOTE: The high-level part is `ret & 0xFF80`, which names the module (e.g. CIPHER)... The low-level part is `ret & ~0xFF80`... the joined form `HIGH : LOW`, e.g. `CIPHER - Authentication failed (for AEAD modes)`.
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer explains the high-level module and low-level parts of the code and that both are rendered joined with " : " when both are present.
